text: The P4 contract story RWB-P4-E1037-CON fixes the operation IDs, request and response bodies, status codes and error model of POST /authorise, GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and GET /masking-policies; v5 carries the operation names and the three inputs Architecture v5 slide 14 names.
why: Architecture v5 names the operations but no source gives a body, a status code or an error model.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet
applied_in: Authorise contract A1, A9 and A10
impact: Sets the contract every service builds against; a change here changes all 19 consumers.

text: /me/permissions is the contract name of the sign-in read and /me/session is its API Specification v4 name; the two are one operation.
why: Architecture v5 outranks the story masters and the API catalogue under the source precedence of Template and Rules R3, and both names read the same roles.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet
impact: One operation instead of two; the API catalogue is corrected at the contract story.

text: A service refreshes its cached permissions on AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged, and refuses an action when rwb-access does not answer inside 2 s or the circuit is open (fail closed); the cache lifetime is left to the contract story and the 5 minute membership refresh the access story assumes under DL38 is the only timing value in a source.
why: Architecture v5 states the cache, the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker but not the lifetime or the outcome of a failed call.
read: Architecture v5 slide 35; slide 43 additions row; access story RWB-E1-037 flow step 11 (DL38)
applied_in: Authorise contract A9 step 3, A10 and A11
impact: A wrong reading either denies valid work during an outage or lets a stale policy stand.

text: The DoA limit amounts stay in the Delegation of Authority Matrix and in the versioned DoA rule package; delegation_limit in rwb_access holds them and GET /doa-limits serves them.
why: No amount, loss percentage or product limit is stated in this workbook.
read: Ownership Map v1 Tables (delegation_limit); Temporal and Drools design DoA notes
applied_in: Authorise contract A6 and A9 step 5
impact: Approval routing stays data-driven and no amount is duplicated in a document.

text: Masking rules are held in rwb_access.masking_rule, owned by P4, set by Compliance under DL26 and served by GET /masking-policies; v5 copies no rule.
why: The workbook states that masking exists but not which role sees which field group in clear.
read: Ownership Map v1 Tables (masking_rule); access story RWB-E1-037 preconditions and BR6
impact: Personal data appears masked until Compliance loads a version.

text: The seven PT roles keep their role rows, letters and default scope with P4; the partner user, the instruction and the result stay with S9 rwb-partner, which holds the user-to-role link and asks POST /authorise with the PT role code.
why: The Ownership Map splits partner users (S9) from the internal role model (P4) and no source states the link.
read: Ownership Map v1 Tables and Rulings (partner_user); Architecture v5 slide 41; Roles tab PT rows
applied_in: Area owners note; Authorise contract A11
impact: The partner portal sign-in path and the S9 contract.

text: The access log is a P4 table in rwb_access, append-only, created by the P4 DB story RWB-P4-E1039-DB, and it is not itemised in the Ownership Map Tables sheet.
why: Architecture v5 names the log and the read operation, and the Ownership Map has no row for it.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Tables; split_plan legacy RWB-E1-039 slices
applied_in: Authorise contract A1 and A6; Access flow Break-glass step 3
impact: The DB story creates a table the Ownership Map does not carry; the register should be updated.

text: The six SY actors are authorised on the same path as a bank role, with their managed identity as the subject and their SY role code; the credential is a client credential over mTLS, as Architecture v5 slide 35 requires of service-to-service calls.
why: The matrix gives each of them a permission row but no source states their credential or their call path.
read: Single sign-on tab; Architecture v5 slide 35
impact: The non-human call path; if the reading is wrong the six actors need a separate contract.

text: The Counts grid stays blank as v4 leaves it; the class totals of the Roles tab note (37, 7, 4 and 6) are confirmed and restated in the Read me sheet and no per-release count is produced.
why: Three role classes hold values that are not an E number, so the release columns cannot be counted without a reading rule.
read: Counts tab; Roles tab; Read me sheet of v5
applied_in: Read me sheet, Counts of this version
impact: Documentation only; no business value changes.

text: The scope values of this document are Own, Team, All and Placed cases, as the Key tab lists them; REGION is not added in v5.
why: The Key tab of the document outranks the story master under R-PREC, and the realignment does not need a new scope value.
read: Key tab Scope rows; access story RWB-E1-037 BR5 and section 12
applied_in: Authorise contract A9 step 4; Read me open points
impact: If a region predicate is needed, the P3 and P4 designs add it and the Key tab is revised then.

text: v5 is issued as Draft because no status and no approval is recorded for v4; the application owner is the approving role.
why: D-RCV-60 issues the next version of every document without waiting for an approval that no source records.
read: Roles tab note row; Key tab Version row
applied_in: Read me sheet, Status line and open point 11
impact: Document control only; no business value changes.
